record_type_quote: Does feeling a warm object make people perceive other people as “warmer” or behave more “warmly” toward them? Williams and Bargh (2008), henceforth WB, reported that participants who held a cup of hot coffee or a hot therapeutic pad perceived others as having warmer personalities and behaved more prosocially than did participants who held a cold object. Feeling physical warmth purportedly primed the construct of interpersonal warmth, thereby changing interpersonal judgments and behaviors. We conducted two high-powered attempts to replicate these results.

targets.title: Experiencing physical warmth promotes interpersonal warmth

Williams and Bargh (2008), henceforth WB, reported that participants who held a cup of hot coffee or a hot therapeutic pad perceived others as having warmer personalities and behaved more prosocially than did participants who held a cold object. targets.outcome_quote: Across two field experiments, we found evidence against WB’s conclusions that physical warmth influences judgments of interpersonal warmth (Experiment 1) and prosocial behavior (Experiment 2).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors give an overall verdict against both original warmth effects. Agreement on control traits and manipulation checks does not change that verdict.
